findings.title: New Finding field uses `.optional()` instead of `.nullish()`
findings.rationale: House rule 1: fields in `Finding` must use `.nullish()`, not `.optional()`, because the schema is sent with `strict: true` and the reviewer model must produce a value for every property. `.optional()` forces the model to invent a value (causing a console warning), while `.nullish()` lets it answer `null`. The new `related_finding_ids` field uses `.optional()`.

findings.rationale: House rule 1: `Review` and `Finding` schemas are also the strict-mode JSON schema the reviewer model fills in. A field marked `.optional()` is required by strict mode, so the model must produce a value and will invent one, emitting a console warning. The repo convention is `.nullish()` (see `server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts:56`). The added line `related_finding_ids: z.array(z.string()).optional(),` should be `.nullish()` to match. This is a warning, not a break: today's callers (all agents) don't set the field, and the model warning is the only symptom.

findings.title: Client copy adds the field but no client code consumes it
findings.rationale: The PR description says the findings panel 'silently ignores it until a later PR adds the UI to actually render the links.' That means the client copy of the contract now carries a field that no client code reads or sets. This is dead contract surface — it compiles, but it is not exercised by any client path. It is not a breaking change (the field is optional), so it is a SUGGESTION rather than a WARNING. The two copies are changed identically, so rule 2 is satisfied.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer returns full detail — breaks callers that rely on the previous contract

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer returns full detail — breaks callers that rely on the previous contract
findings.rationale: The diff changes GET /pulls/:id from a live fetch that returns the full detail (files, commits, diff stats) to a pure read of the stored row. Any caller that previously relied on GET /pulls/:id to return the full detail (e.g. the Pull Requests list page that backfilled filesCount from the detail fetch, or any external consumer) will now receive a partial response. The new POST /pulls/:id/refresh is a new route that must be called to get the full detail, but the client was updated to use it. However, the server route still returns the same PrDetail shape, so the client-side change is consistent. The breaking change is the removal of the live-fetch behavior from GET, which is a behavioral contract change that could break other callers that did not update. The compatible alternative is to keep GET /pulls/:id returning the full detail (or at least the same shape as before) and add the new refresh endpoint as an optional enhancement, or to version the new behavior behind a query parameter.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer returns the full PR detail — breaks existing callers

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer returns the full PR detail — breaks existing callers
findings.rationale: The diff removes the live GitHub fetch and the backfill of filesCount/commitsCount from GET /pulls/:id, and instead returns only the stored row (id, number, title, etc.). The new POST /pulls/:id/refresh is required to populate the detail. Any existing caller that does GET /pulls/:id and expects the full detail (files, commits, body, diff stats) will now get a reduced payload and no live data. This is a breaking change for the web client and any external consumer. The compatible alternative is to keep GET /pulls/:id returning the full detail (either by keeping the live fetch or by returning the stored detail plus a flag), and add the refresh endpoint as an optional enhancement.

matched_title: POST /pulls/:id/refresh returns raw GitHub detail, not PrDetail — client refresh breaks

findings.title: POST /pulls/:id/refresh returns raw GitHub detail, not PrDetail — client refresh breaks
findings.rationale: The new refresh route returns the raw GitHub detail payload (snake_case fields, no id) instead of the PrDetail shape the client's POST /pulls/:id/refresh call expects. The client's mutationFn does api.post<PrDetail>(`/pulls/${prId}/refresh`) and then reads the result as PrDetail (e.g. pr.id, pr.files). With the raw payload, the client gets undefined for id and snake_case fields, so the refresh flow fails at runtime. This is a CRITICAL contract break for the new refresh button.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id response shape changed — existing client page breaks
findings.rationale: The GET /pulls/:id handler previously returned the stored PrDetail (with id, camelCase fields). The diff changes it to return the raw GitHub detail object (snake_case, no id). The existing client page (client/src/app/repos/[repoId]/pulls/[number]/page.tsx) reads pr.id and other PrDetail fields; with the new shape it gets undefined for id and snake_case fields, so the page breaks. This is a CRITICAL contract break for the existing PR detail page.

findings.title: Shared contract copies not both updated
findings.rationale: The diff changes the pulls contract (new refresh route, changed GET response) under server/src/vendor/shared/ but does not update the corresponding client/src/vendor/shared/ copy. Per the house rules, a shared contract change must be mirrored in both copies; otherwise the client silently drifts from the server contract.

findings.title: Client refresh throws plain Error instead of ApiError
findings.rationale: The new refresh mutation in PrDetailHeader calls api.post directly and, on a non-2xx response, throws a plain Error instead of an ApiError. Per the house rules, client code that calls the engine with fetch directly must throw ApiError on non-2xx so the page can show the server's message/status/code. A plain Error loses that context.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id response shape changed — breaks callers reading files/commits/diff stats

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id response shape changed — breaks callers reading files/commits/diff stats
findings.rationale: The old GET /pulls/:id handler returned { ...detail, id: pr.id } where detail was the full GitHub payload including files, commits, files_count, and diff stats. The new handler returns a stored subset { id, number, title, ... } with no files/commits/diff stats. Any deployed caller (web client PR detail page, e2e flows, CI) that reads detail.files, detail.commits, or detail.files_count from the GET response now silently gets undefined/empty. This is a breaking contract change for existing callers.

matched_title: Refresh route returns snake_case GitHub payload, breaking the camelCase contract

findings.title: Refresh route returns snake_case GitHub payload, breaking the camelCase contract
findings.rationale: The new POST /pulls/:id/refresh handler returns the raw GitHub detail object (detail) after backfilling files/commits. GitHub's payload uses snake_case (files_count, additions, deletions, etc.), but the existing GET /pulls/:id response and the client's PrDetail type use camelCase (filesCount, additions, deletions). The client's mutationFn reads the response as PrDetail, so filesCount, additions, deletions, and other camelCase fields will be undefined after a refresh. This breaks the contract for the new endpoint and for any caller that uses the response.

findings.title: Client refresh fetch throws plain Error, losing ApiError contract
findings.rationale: The new mutationFn calls api.post<PrDetail>(`/pulls/${prId}/refresh`). If the server returns a non-2xx (e.g. 404, 422, 500), the client's api.post helper throws a plain Error instead of an ApiError. The client's error-handling code (e.g. pages that check error instanceof ApiError) will show a generic message and lose the server's error code and message. This violates the house rule that client requests surface errors as ApiError.
